page.overview:
Who is Chaeryu?

As a teenager, Chaeryu fell in love with Lady Huazo of the Saowon clan, taking her as his mistress. They would often retreat from the pressures of the royal court, venturing to the countryside. Chaeryu greatly enjoyed these trips, as they distanced him from the weight and boredom of politics. However, he and Huazo would often bicker due to the trips, as Chaeryu took little interest in preparing them and thought that they would do fine without equipment. In contrast, his mistress believed it foolish to venture into the wilds without anything and often had to handle all of the preparations on her own.

Huazo was not well-received as a royal mistress, and Chaeryu became convinced that he could do better than her. During a royal garden party, he was introduced to Lady Sulan of the Keohso clan and was immediately smitten with her. Although this provided a great opportunity to end his relationship with Huazo, it turned into a great embarrassment for him when Huazo revealed she was pregnant with his first child, Chaejin.

Chaeryu later married Lady Sulan, who fell pregnant with Chaeryu's second son, Zoryu. Although she was considered a wonderful person by many, others believed her to be hopelessly naive. She convinced Chaeryu to name their son Zoryu, whose name used a character that was traditional to the Saowon clan. This caused great offense to the Saowon, but Sulan had not intended any slight, merely believing the name sounded nice. Sulan died giving birth to Zoryu. After Sulan's death, Chaeryu took several more mistresses, and Zoryu later suspected that he had many more illegitimate siblings. Unlike Huazo, however, none of these later mistresses had a high rank, and their children were not officially acknowledged as his.

Chaeryu's two known sons were playmates to each other in their youth. After ascending the throne, Chaeryu decided to exclude his illegitimate son from the royal family and the line of succession. Chaejin was sent away from court to live with the Fire Sages and Chaeryu forbade anyone to speak on the matter as long as he lived.
